NC500: Scotland's Ultimate Motorcycle Route

The North Coast 500 is Britain's answer to Route 66 — a 516-mile loop around the Scottish Highlands that takes in some of the most spectacular scenery and finest motorcycle roads in Europe. Our illustrated map highlights the 10 essential stops every biker should make.

Key Stats

  • Total Distance: 516 miles
  • Recommended Riding Days: 3–5 (don't rush it)
  • Best Months: May to September
  • Fuel Planning: Fill up every 80 miles — remote sections have limited stations

The 10 Must-Stop Locations

  1. Inverness — Start and finish point. Stock up on supplies and fuel.
  2. Black Isle — Rolling farmland and dolphin-watching at Chanonry Point.
  3. Dunrobin Castle — Fairy-tale castle with falconry displays.
  4. John O'Groats — The iconic northern tip of mainland Britain.
  5. Durness — Remote beauty with Smoo Cave and stunning beaches.
  6. Ullapool — Charming harbour town, perfect overnight stop.
  7. Bealach na Ba — The UK's best motorcycle road. 2,053ft of Alpine-grade hairpins.
  8. Applecross — Reward yourself at the Applecross Inn after the Bealach.
  9. Torridon — Wild mountain scenery at its finest.
  10. Loch Ness — Keep an eye out for Nessie on the final stretch home.

keyTakeaways: The North Coast 500 is a 516-mile loop around the Scottish Highlands starting and finishing in Inverness.
Allow three to five riding days rather than rushing the route in one weekend.
The best riding months are May to September for weather and open facilities.
Fuel is sparse in the far north, so fill up roughly every 80 miles.
Bealach na Ba is the route's highlight, with 2,053ft of Alpine-grade hairpins.

faq.q: How many days do you need to ride the NC500?
faq.a: Three to five days is ideal. Riding the full 516 miles in one or two days leaves no time for the coastline, castles and cafes that make the route special, and the roads are demanding enough that fatigue becomes a safety issue. Spreading it over several days lets you enjoy the Highlands properly.

faq.q: When is the best time to ride the NC500?
faq.a: May to September offers the longest daylight, the mildest weather and the widest choice of open accommodation and fuel stops. Midges peak in high summer, so late spring and early autumn are popular sweet spots. Avoid winter, when snow, ice and short daylight make the remote sections risky.

faq.q: How do you plan fuel stops on the NC500?
faq.a: Fill up roughly every 80 miles and never pass a station you might need in the far north-west. Some remote pumps have limited hours or card-only payment, so plan around the settlements at Ullapool, Durness and Tongue. Filling at half a tank in remote areas is a sensible rule.

faq.q: Which is the best road on the NC500?
faq.a: Bealach na Ba on the Applecross peninsula is the standout. It climbs 2,053ft with Alpine-grade hairpins and huge views, and is widely rated the best motorcycle road in the UK. It is single-track with passing places, so ride steadily and enjoy the Applecross Inn as a reward.

faq.q: Is the NC500 suitable for beginners?
faq.a: Confident riders with some touring experience will manage it, but the single-track sections, blind crests, passing places and remote distances make it challenging. Newer riders should build slow-control skills first, keep daily distances modest and carry breakdown cover, as help can be a long way off.
